chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does there happen something today which was not in the Knowledge of Allah yesterday? He said: No. May the one who says that be abased by Allah. I said: Consider whatever has happened and whatever will happen up to the Day of Judgment - is it not in the knowledge of Allah? He said: Yes. Before He created the creation.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Divine Knowledge and temporal events in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi addresses the theological concept of divine foreknowledge by affirming that all temporal events, past and future, were already encompassed in Allah's eternal knowledge prior to creation. It specifically refutes the notion that God's knowledge is static or limited to the past, establishing a coherent Shia understanding of how the eternal divine intellect interacts with temporal unfolding. This clarification supports the doctrine of 'Ilm al-Ghayb' (Knowledge of the Unseen) as an intrinsic attribute of God rather than a cumulative acquisition.

en.ammaar-muslim: 7. [7/344] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from Muhammad b. Isa from Yunus from Mansur b. Hazim who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام: Does there happen something today which was not in the Knowledge of Allah yesterday? He said: No. May the one who says that be abased by Allah. I said: Consider whatever has happened and whatever will happen up to the Day of Judgment - is it not in the knowledge of Allah? He said: Yes. Before He created the creation.
